pr.title: Remove redundant semicolon from generated resolver (REQ-2204)
pr.body:
Requirement: REQ-2204

Agent-written implementation of requirement REQ-2204 (upstream MessagePack-CSharp issue 2204), from the Junction 2026 challenge branch `ju26-issue-2204`.

Author: coding agent. Accountable owner: to be assigned by Countersign.
pr.author: ToukoUrsin

requirement.title: Redundant extra semicolon in the generated file (causing warning in some development tools)

criteria.text: For a compilation with custom IMessagePackFormatter<> types, the generated MessagePackResolverGetFormatterHelper.GetFormatter() method has no semicolon right after the closing brace of the switch statement.
criteria.sourceQuote: Generated MessagePackResolverGetFormatterHelper.GetFormatter() method contains an extra `;` after the switch statement, which is redundant.
criteria.note: Runs MessagePackGenerator on the repro (two custom IMessagePackFormatter<> types plus a [GeneratedMessagePackResolver]) and checks that no switch in the generated GetFormatterHelper.GetFormatter has a ';' token or empty statement right after its closing brace, and that the text has no `};` after the default branch.

criteria.text: The generated GetFormatter() switch still has one `case N: return new <FormatterType>();` per entry in closedTypeLookup plus the `default: return null;` branch, so the same formatter instances are returned for each type as before.
criteria.sourceQuote: While no impact on compiled code
criteria.note: Parses the generated helper and checks that each closedTypeLookup entry index has exactly one matching `case N: return new ...;` section, that SomeTypeNameFormatter and OtherTypeNameFormatter are both constructed, and that there is a `default: return null;` section.

criteria.text: Wherever the template emits a switch statement (both template locations the requirement points to), the generated resolver source has no empty statement (`;`) directly after the switch's closing brace.
criteria.note: Generates a resolver with both closed custom formatters and an open-generic formatter, checks that both the closedKey and openKey switches are emitted, and checks that no switch in any generated tree is followed by an empty statement or ';'.

criteria.text: The generated resolver file still compiles with no new compiler errors or warnings, and the snapshot/verified files for the generated resolver source are updated so they no longer contain the `};` after the switch.
criteria.note: Compiles the input together with the generated sources for the closed and open-generic formatter case, and checks that the generated trees produce no compiler warnings or errors.

criteria.text: All existing source generator and resolver tests still pass, and any snapshot changes are only the removed semicolon, with no other unrelated differences.
criteria.note: Supported by the regression run only; no test targets this criterion specifically.

criteria.text: Generated output for code with no custom formatters, or with only generic or open-generic formatter lookups, behaves the same as before apart from the removed semicolon.
criteria.note: For a compilation with only a [MessagePackObject] type and no custom formatters, checks that the generated resolver compiles without errors, emits no openKey switch, and that GetFormatter still ends with `return null;`.

story.headline: The generated MessagePackResolverGetFormatterHelper.GetFormatter() method no longer has a stray `;` after its switch statements.
story.before: Both switch statements in the generated GetFormatter (the closed-type lookup and the open-generic lookup) ended with `};`. The extra semicolon is an empty statement after a switch that always returns. ReSharper and similar tools flagged it as unreachable code in every user project with a custom formatter.
story.after: Both switches now end with `}`. The emitted code compiles the same as before and no longer contains the empty statement.

steps.text: In ResolverTemplate.tt, the `;` after the closing brace of the closedKey switch (line 75) and the openKey switch (line 88) is removed.
ResolverTemplate.cs, the T4-generated C# that MessagePackGenerator.Emit runs through TransformText, gets the same two string edits so the generator actually emits the new text.
The 90 verified resolver snapshot files in the source generator tests are updated from `};` to `}` so snapshot comparison matches the new output.

alsoTouches: Generated resolver source changes for every user project that uses the source generator and has formatter registrations, not only projects with custom IMessagePackFormatter types.
The open-generic switch (formatters created via Activator.CreateInstance) loses its trailing `;` too, which goes beyond the closed-type example in the report.

diagrams.title: Removing the trailing semicolon from the generated resolver switch
diagrams.caption: The only change is to template text; anything that runs ResolverTemplate.TransformText emits slightly different source, and the snapshots are updated to match.
